Desk Organisers/Table Organizer (breadcrumb 'Study room furniture') = functional office organizer, excluded. Cutlery Holders, Chopping Board, Jars (breadcrumb 'Kitchenware/Storage containers'), Kitchenware = functional kitchen tools/storage, excluded. Soap Dispenser Sets, Bathroom Accessories, Towels = bathroom/textile, excluded. Wall Organizers, Wall Shelves, Laundry Baskets = storage furniture, excluded. WallPaper = explicit exclusion. Spiritual/Home Temple/Pooja Essentials/Chowki/Wall-Mounted Pooja Mandir = religious furniture (also mostly dead links), excluded. Chandelier Fans = ceiling-fan exclusion. DEAD LINKS (verified 404 via probe + curl, real absence per Rule 3, simply omitted rather than fabricated): /bathroom-mirrors, /wall-plates, /wall-masks, /metal-wall-arts, /glassware, /platters, /plates, /coffee-mugs, /teapots, /candles, /religious-idol, /door-hanging. OVERLAP judgment calls: Vases (51) already subsumes its 'Flower Vase' sub-filter (43 of 51, breadcrumb-nested, classic subset) so Flower Vase was NOT added as a second row to avoid double-counting. Ceiling Lights (20) and Pendant Lights (28) are breadcrumb-nested (Lighting > Ceiling Lights > Pendant Lights) but Pendant Lights' own count exceeds Ceiling Lights' own count, proving they are independently curated listings rather than a clean subset, so both were kept as sibling leaf rows (flagging the possible partial overlap here for the record). Table Showpiece (47) and Figurines (38) are separate site catalog nodes under Home Decor with some titles that look similar (decorative showpieces) - kept as two rows since each has its own independently-reported exact count and there is no subset evidence between them. Hub/aggregate pages (/home-decors, /lighting, /lamps-and-lighting, /wall-decor, /wall-arts, /clocks, /table-decor, /tableware, /mirrors) show their OWN small curated counts that do not equal the sum of their children (parent pages here are curated marketing subsets, not the union) - these were used only as parent:true structural rows (qty null), never as a qty source, per Rule 1.
